meetings.title: Booking project kickoff
meetings.overview: The team kicked off the online booking project for the clinic network. They agreed scope, the vendor and a first go-live target. Several tasks were handed out.
keyPoints: All 12 clinics go live on April 8
decisions: Go live at all 12 clinics on April 8
Sign the vendor contract with Calloway Soft

actions.task: Register the sender name for text reminders
Build the insurance eligibility check
Write the patient consent text
Sign the vendor contract
Register the booking domain name

openQuestions: Do we need booking forms in other languages?

say.text: Thanks everyone. This is the kickoff for online booking at Harrowgate. The goal is simple: patients book, move and cancel visits without calling.
The vendor contract with Calloway Soft is ready. I will sign it this week, then we have a vendor.
Front desks take around 400 calls a day across the network. If we cut half of that, staff get time back for patients.
I can take the technical side. I already registered the booking domain name, so that is done.
The budget is 180k for the first year. I want to go live at all 12 clinics on April 8, the same day.
April 8 is tight but fine for me. The clinics are quiet that week.
Patients will get a text reminder the day before. For that we need a registered sender name, so I will start that request.
Good. We also need the insurance eligibility check, so the system tells the patient if the visit is covered.
That one is the big integration. I will start with the payer interface and see how far I get by Feb 10.
One idea from the desks: a waitlist, so a freed slot goes to the next person. I do not know how hard it is.
Park the waitlist for now. We will come back after the basics.
Also patients must accept a consent text before they book. Someone needs to write it.
I will write the consent text and send it to legal by Jan 30.
What about patients who do not speak English? Many in the east clinics prefer Spanish or Somali.
Good question. Let us keep it as an open question for the next meeting.

meetings.title: Insurance and reminders review
meetings.overview: The team reviewed progress on reminders, insurance checks and the consent text. Some items are waiting on outside parties. The group agreed to start the work on the language forms.
keyPoints: Reminder sender name still not registered
Insurance check waiting on an outside party
Front desk training to be planned
decisions: Build forms in Spanish and Somali first

actions.task: Get the reminder sender name registered
Get a payer sandbox key for the eligibility check
Get legal approval for the consent text
Build Spanish and Somali booking forms
Order kiosk tablets for the clinics

openQuestions: Who pays for the translation of the forms?

say.text: Quick status round. The sender name for the reminders first, Rashid.
Not registered yet. The request needs a signature from the board treasurer, and she is on leave until March 3.
Understood. What about the insurance side?
The payer is NorthStar Mutual. They only give us sandbox keys after we sign a data sharing agreement, and their lawyers say that takes 30 days.
I can push on the legal side with them. Send me the draft.
The consent text went to counsel Bram Oyelaran last week. He wants it under 300 words, so I have to cut it down.
The kiosk tablets arrived at all clinics, so that item is done. Front desk staff still need training before the pilot.
Mei-Ling, can you plan the training sessions? Two hours per clinic should be enough.
Yes, I will draft a plan by Feb 24. Also, I still think the waitlist should be in the first release.
We said we park it. Let us keep that for now.
About the language question from last time. The east clinics need Spanish and Somali forms.
I can build both forms in the vendor tool. The translation text must come from somebody else.
Then we start with Spanish and Somali and ask who pays for the translation.
Finance said maybe the clinic budget. Nobody confirmed it.
OK. We write that as an open question.

meetings.title: Pilot plan and record migration
meetings.overview: The team turned the rollout into a pilot first. New items came up around old records and the phone line. Reminders are still not moving.
keyPoints: Old appointment records need to move
decisions: Pilot at 3 clinics on April 8, the other 9 clinics in June

actions.task: Fix and resubmit the sender request for reminders
Get the insurance lookup passing in the sandbox
Migrate the old appointment records into the new system
Write the phone line cutover script
Finish the front desk training plan

openQuestions: Should the pediatric clinics get separate calendars?
Which clinics join the pilot first?

say.text: Vendor call yesterday. Calloway Soft says 12 clinics at the same time is too much for their support team.
So they proposed a pilot first. Three clinics on April 8, and the other nine in June.
I agree. We take a pilot at 3 clinics on April 8 and the rest in June.
Good for me. Now the reminders. The carrier rejected our sender request because the tax id on the form did not match their file.
So we resubmit it with the right tax id.
Yes, I need the number from finance first. Also, the insurance lookup in the sandbox is not passing yet.
New topic. We must move the old appointment records into the new system. The front desks use them every day.
I can do it, but I need a plan. I will take it with a due date of March 10.
Another item is the phone line. When patients call the old number, we need a script that tells them about the new booking site. I will write the cutover script.
The pediatric clinics do not agree on the calendar layout. Three want separate calendars and two want to share with the general clinic.
That needs a decision, but not today.
On the consent text, counsel now says the state privacy rule changes on April 1, and he wants to wait for the final wording.
So the legal sign-off is waiting again.
Yes. I will chase him next week.
Should the waitlist stay out? Mei-Ling asked again.
It goes to phase 2 for now.

meetings.title: Waitlist and sandbox problems
meetings.overview: The group looked at sandbox problems and brought the waitlist back. Two older items are still waiting. A security test was booked.
decisions: The waitlist moves into the pilot

actions.task: Resubmit the sender request for reminders with a new name
Get the insurance lookup passing in the sandbox
Migrate the old appointment records
Run the penetration test of the booking site
Finish the front desk training plan

openQuestions: Who approves the cost of the Somali forms?

say.text: Let's start with the sandbox. Rashid?
The Calloway sandbox returns a 504 error when I send a batch of 200 requests. Their engineer says a fix is due on March 25.
So the insurance lookup waits for that.
Yes. And the sender request: the carrier says the name HARROWGATE is already registered by a clinic in another state. We must choose a new name.
Pick something short. I will ask the board.
On the old appointment records, I tried the export. The old system's export tool breaks after 40,000 rows, and we have 190,000 rows.
So we need another way to pull the data.
I booked the penetration test for the booking site. The tester asks for a stable build first.
Now the waitlist. I want it in the pilot, not in phase 2. Last quarter 212 slots went empty because of late cancellations, and a waitlist would have filled maybe half of them.
That is a strong number. Mei-Ling has pushed for this since the start, so let's do it.
It adds about a week of work for me.
Accepted. The waitlist moves into the pilot.
The phone line cutover script is half done. I will finish after the pen test.
The front desk training plan is done. I sent it to all clinic managers. Also, the agency quoted 1,900 dollars for the Somali forms, and finance has not approved it.
The consent text is still waiting for counsel. Nothing new there.

meetings.title: Pilot readiness check
meetings.overview: The final review before the pilot. The pilot start moved again and the plan changed in several places. Many items stay open and the project lead changes.
keyPoints: Pilot start moved to May 13 at 2 clinics
Rashid takes over as project lead
Text reminders move to Tidewell Messaging
decisions: Pilot moves to May 13 at 2 clinics
Use Tidewell Messaging for text reminders

actions.task: Register a sender id with Tidewell Messaging
Get the insurance lookup passing in the sandbox
Migrate the old appointment records
Run the penetration test
Test the waitlist feature

openQuestions: Will the pediatric clinics share one calendar?
Will counsel sign before the pilot?

say.text: Before we start: Hannelore moves to the finance project next week, and Rashid takes over as project lead.
Fine with me. The budget also changes. The vendor asked for extra work on the waitlist, so we are now at 214k.
I signed it off yesterday.
The pilot cannot start on April 8. The new date is May 13, and we start with only 2 clinics.
That is fine for the front desks. They need more time anyway. The training plan is closed, both pilot clinics finished their sessions.
On reminders: we switch to Tidewell Messaging. They need 10 business days to approve a new sender id.
So no reminders at the pilot start?
Only if they approve on time.
The insurance lookup still does not pass. The billing lead found that 3 of 11 insurance plans use a different member id format.
That needs a mapping table.
For the old appointment records, I found 6,300 duplicate patient records. We must clean them before the import.
The pediatric clinics still want separate calendars. The group of three did not change its mind.
The pen test is booked for April 30. The phone line cutover script comes after.
The legal sign-off is the last one on my list. Counsel signs only after the state rule is final.
The waitlist is built but not tested. I will test it by May 5.

meetings.title: Abertura da migração dos registros
meetings.overview: A reunião abriu o projeto de migração dos registros escolares da rede para o novo sistema. O grupo definiu o escopo, o fornecedor e uma data para desligar o sistema antigo. Várias tarefas foram distribuídas.
keyPoints: A rede tem 48 escolas e cerca de 310 mil registros
Sistema antigo será desligado em 30 de junho
Migração das 48 escolas de uma vez
Congelar o lançamento de notas foi sugerido
decisions: Migrar todas as 48 escolas de uma vez
Desligar o servidor antigo em 30 de junho

actions.task: Fazer o inventário das escolas
Fechar o contrato com a Datamar
Importar o histórico de notas
Importar as guias de transferência
Organizar o treinamento das secretarias

openQuestions: O que fazer com os registros de alunos que saíram antes de 2005?

say.text: Bom dia a todos. Hoje abrimos a migração dos registros escolares para o novo sistema, o Cadastro Único.
Nossa rede tem 48 escolas e mais ou menos 310 mil registros de alunos.
O inventário das escolas já está pronto. Visitei todas as unidades no mês passado.
O contrato com a Datamar também foi fechado. Então temos fornecedor.
Meu plano é migrar as 48 escolas de uma vez. O servidor antigo desliga no dia 30 de junho.
Prefiro assim, uma data só. Mas o histórico de notas é o item mais pesado.
O sistema antigo exporta as notas em texto, e os acentos quebram na importação. Nomes como João viram caracteres estranhos.
Entendi. Então importar o histórico de notas fica aberto por enquanto.
Também temos as guias de transferência. Cada aluno que muda de escola tem uma.
Eu cuido das guias de transferência também, para março.
As secretárias das escolas precisam de treinamento antes da virada. Eu organizo o treinamento das secretarias.
Uma ideia: congelar o lançamento de notas durante a cópia dos dados. Mas não sei se as escolas aceitam.
Vamos pensar nisso. Fica para a próxima reunião.
E os alunos que saíram antes de 2005? Não sei se devemos guardar esses registros.
Boa pergunta. Fica como pergunta aberta.

meetings.title: Duplicatas e prazo de guarda
meetings.overview: O grupo avaliou os primeiros testes de importação. Surgiram problemas com os dados e o plano de migração mudou. O treinamento das secretarias também foi discutido.
keyPoints: Plano mudou para ondas por região
Treinamento das secretarias ainda sem data
Prazo de guarda dos registros antigos sem resposta
Guias de transferência ainda não importadas
decisions: Migrar em três ondas por região em vez de tudo de uma vez

actions.task: Remover os CPF duplicados dos alunos
Refazer a importação do histórico de notas
Importar as guias de transferência
Marcar as datas do treinamento das secretarias
Perguntar ao conselho estadual o prazo de guarda

openQuestions: Quanto tempo devemos guardar os registros antigos?

say.text: Vamos ver os testes de importação. Joselito, como foi?
Rodei a primeira importação em três escolas. Achei 6.800 alunos com CPF duplicado no cadastro antigo.
Isso trava a importação. O novo sistema não aceita dois alunos com o mesmo CPF.
Eu preciso limpar essas duplicatas antes. Levo uns quinze dias.
Com isso, acho que migrar as 48 escolas de uma vez é arriscado.
Concordo. Proponho três ondas por região: norte, centro e sul.
Fechado. Três ondas por região.
Sobre o treinamento das secretarias, a Secretaria de Finanças só libera o pagamento dos instrutores depois de 3 de junho.
Então sem instrutor contratado não dá para marcar datas.
Isso mesmo. Vou tentar usar instrutores da própria rede.
As guias de transferência estão paradas. Precisam do histórico de notas pronto antes.
Sobre os registros de quem saiu antes de 2005: a lei fala em prazo de guarda, mas há dúvida se são 20 ou 50 anos.
Vou perguntar ao conselho estadual.
Eles costumam demorar.
Eu sei. Vamos registrar como pergunta aberta.

meetings.title: Ondas e congelamento de notas
meetings.overview: O grupo detalhou as ondas da migração e tratou do congelamento do lançamento de notas. Os testes dependem de um ambiente que ainda não está liberado. O treinamento segue sem solução.
keyPoints: Congelamento do lançamento de notas aprovado
Ambiente para testes ainda não liberado
Pergunta sobre registros antigos continua sem resposta
decisions: Congelar o lançamento de notas durante a cópia de cada onda

actions.task: Limpar os CPF duplicados
Refazer a importação do histórico de notas
Importar as guias de alunos
Preparar a formação nas escolas rurais
Avisar as escolas sobre o congelamento de notas

openQuestions: Quem paga o transporte do treinamento nas escolas rurais?
Qual o prazo de guarda dos registros antigos?

say.text: Hoje quero fechar as ondas e falar do congelamento de notas.
Eu defendo o congelamento desde a primeira reunião. No ano passado, durante a exportação, 1.900 notas foram alteradas depois da cópia, e ninguém percebeu.
Joselito tem razão. Com notas mudando, a cópia nunca fica certa.
Concordo. Congelamos o lançamento durante a cópia de cada onda, por uma semana.
Aprovado. Eu aviso as escolas até 5 de abril e esse item já está feito.
Sobre o histórico de notas: a prefeitura só libera o servidor de testes depois do dia 18 de maio, então não consigo testar a importação completa antes.
Mas dá para testar com um lote pequeno.
Dá, mas não vale como teste final.
No treinamento, temos 14 escolas rurais sem internet. Os instrutores teriam de ir até lá, e isso custa mais.
Podemos fazer a formação em um polo, uma escola central da região.
Boa. Mas ainda falta saber quem paga o transporte.
As ondas ficam assim: norte em 2 de junho, centro em 16 de junho e sul em 30 de junho.
Isso aperta o prazo do servidor antigo.
Vamos ver isso na próxima.
Ainda sem resposta do conselho estadual sobre o prazo de guarda.

meetings.title: Revisão de prontidão
meetings.overview: A última reunião revisou a prontidão da migração. O plano mudou de novo e o prazo do servidor antigo foi movido. Alguns itens seguem abertos.
keyPoints: Servidor antigo será desligado em 15 de setembro
Total de registros subiu para 340 mil
decisions: Migrar primeiro as 12 escolas do ensino médio
Desligar o servidor antigo em 15 de setembro

actions.task: Limpar os CPF duplicados que faltam
Importar as guias de transferência
Resolver a formação das secretarias rurais
Cobrar resposta do conselho estadual
Assinar o contrato com a Infoserra

openQuestions: Os registros de quem saiu antes de 2005 serão guardados por 20 ou 50 anos?

say.text: Revisão final. Primeiro, as notícias: a Datamar saiu do projeto e o novo fornecedor é a Infoserra.
O contrato com a Infoserra já foi assinado, então esse item está feito.
A segunda mudança é o plano. Vamos migrar primeiro só as 12 escolas do ensino médio, e o resto depois.
Faz sentido. Com 48 escolas era muita coisa.
O servidor antigo agora desliga em 15 de setembro, não mais em 30 de junho.
A contagem de registros subiu. Agora são 340 mil, porque entraram as matrículas de reforço.
E eu passo a coordenação para o Joselito na semana que vem.
Aceito. A limpeza do CPF duplicado ainda não terminou. Faltam 2.100 casos.
As guias de transferência dependem do formulário novo, e a Infoserra ainda não liberou o modelo da guia.
O treinamento nas escolas rurais continua sem solução, e ainda não sabemos quem paga o transporte.
Para as 12 escolas do ensino médio, a formação pode ser online.
Sobre o prazo de guarda: o conselho estadual respondeu que ainda está avaliando, e não deu data.
Então continua em aberto. A dúvida é entre 20 e 50 anos.
Vamos documentar isso na ata.
Isso. Obrigado a todos.

meetings.title: Fleet upgrade kickoff
meetings.overview: The team started the fleet upgrade for the city bike-share. They agreed the size of the new fleet, the supplier and a launch date. The charging approach was set for a first test.
keyPoints: Battery cells come from Norvane Cells
Charging at the docks as the base plan
decisions: Charge the e-bikes at the docks

actions.task: Survey the pilot routes
Get an insurance quote
Update dock firmware for e-bike charging
Find suppliers for puncture-proof tires
Update the rider app for e-bikes

openQuestions: Can the harbor district get sidewalk docks?
Where can the repair workshop move?

say.text: Welcome to the fleet upgrade kickoff. We replace the old bikes with e-bikes across the Spokewell network.
The plan is 600 e-bikes for the first stage. Battery cells come from Norvane Cells.
The city wants launch on June 1. I have the route survey done, so that item is closed.
I got the insurance quote too. It is done and filed.
For charging, the base plan is to charge at the docks. Every dock needs a firmware update for that.
Can the dock firmware be done by March 20?
I think so. I will own the dock firmware update.
Riders will pay 2.50 per ride for an e-bike. The app must show the battery level, so I take the rider app update.
A nice-to-have: puncture-proof tires. I will look at suppliers, but it costs more per bike.
OK, find suppliers first. We decide later.
The harbor district has no docks yet. The city must allow sidewalk docks there.
That depends on the council. Let's keep it as an open question.
Also the repair workshop is too small for 600 e-bikes.
Noted. We look at it after the battery order.
Agreed.

meetings.title: Battery supply and swap vans
meetings.overview: The team reviewed the battery order and changed the charging plan. The supply schedule is slipping. Work on the app and the docks continues.
decisions: Use battery swap vans instead of charging at the docks

actions.task: Update the firmware on the docks
Buy two swap vans
Update the app for riders
Choose the tire supplier
Check the paperwork for the cells

say.text: Battery status first. The cells from Norvane Cells are late.
Customs holds the shipment. The lithium cells sit at the port with a customs hold since May 2.
How long does the hold last?
Unknown. Customs says it can take up to three weeks.
Because of this, charging at the docks is a problem. The docks need new power lines in many places.
Then use swap vans. A van brings charged batteries to each dock, and takes the empty ones.
I like it. Fewer power lines, less city work.
Decision: battery swap vans, not charging at the docks. We buy two vans.
The app for riders needs a battery-swap alert. That is more work for me, but fine.
The firmware for the docks is still in progress, since the old plan changed a bit.
The tire supplier shortlist is ready. Three options, prices are close.
I still think we should pick puncture-proof.
We decide next time.
The harbor docks wait for the council.
Yes. Nothing to do there for now.

meetings.title: Tire decision and test results
meetings.overview: The group looked at test results for the battery packs and decided the tire question. The workshop plan is still open. The supplier problem continues.
decisions: Buy puncture-proof tires for all e-bikes

actions.task: Test battery packs again after the supplier fix
Update dock firmware
Finish the rider app update
Confirm the swap van service plan
Order two swap vans

openQuestions: Where can the repair workshop move?

say.text: The first battery packs arrived by air. We ran the vibration test, and 3 of 40 packs failed.
That is a second problem on top of the customs hold.
Yes. The supplier says the failures come from the new mounting bracket.
Tamsin, you pushed for puncture-proof tires. Give the reason again.
Last winter we had 340 flat tires in 8 weeks. Each repair costs a van trip and a day without that bike.
That is convincing. Wendell, what is the extra cost?
About 18 per bike. For 600 bikes that is 10,800.
Approved. We buy puncture-proof tires for all e-bikes.
The swap vans are ordered. That item is done.
The council vote on the harbor docks is scheduled for May 21.
So the harbor district stays open until then.
Dock firmware is not finished. I need the final battery data first.
The rider app is nearly done. I need the final alert texts.
We also need a plan for who services the swap vans. The repair workshop is too small.
I can ask the city for a second workshop.
OK. Please do.

meetings.title: Revised fleet plan
meetings.overview: The final review changed the fleet plan again. Size, date and price all moved. Battery supply is still not settled.
keyPoints: Hybrid swap and charge plan for hubs
decisions: Swap at 20 hub docks and charge at the other docks

actions.task: Update dock firmware for hub charging
Finish the rider app update
Find a second repair workshop
Sign the contract with Harlow Cells
Retest battery packs from Harlow Cells

openQuestions: Will the council allow harbor docks?

say.text: Big changes today. We cut the fleet to 450 e-bikes in the first stage.
The cause is the battery supply. Norvane Cells moved production to a new plant on March 9, and the first full delivery slips by two months.
So the launch moves from June 1 to July 14.
And the ride price goes up to 3.10. The cost per bike rose.
We also switch supplier. Harlow Cells will deliver the remaining packs. The contract is signed, so that item is done.
With fewer packs, charging changes again. We swap at 20 hub docks and charge at the other docks.
Fine. Hybrid it is.
Dock firmware has to change for the hub charging. That work is still open.
The rider app update is still open, too. I wait for the hub list.
The repair workshop: we still need a second location.
The city offered nothing yet.
The council vote for the harbor docks is on May 21, so it is still open.
The retest of the battery packs from Harlow Cells starts June 1.
Anything else? No. Thanks.
Thanks all.
